title: Insurance for property trade work in Australia
audience: Owners of small property trade businesses who need to understand what insurance covers before they accept work
learningOutcomes: Identify the insurance types a small property trade business should consider, and describe what each one covers in general terms.
Compare quotes using the same scope of work, the same limits, the same exclusions and the same conditions.
Keep a register of policies, certificates and renewal dates that a client or a regulator can check.

instruction.heading: What insurance is for
instruction.body: Insurance shifts the expense of a serious mistake or accident away from the owner and the client. A tradesperson can damage a client's property while working, and a member of the public can be hurt on a site. Those events can cost far more than a year of premiums. Insurance also builds trust, because many clients, property managers and councils ask for proof of cover before they engage a trade. The guide this lesson draws on describes general liability insurance and workers compensation. The Australian term for cover against claims from third parties for injury or property damage caused by the work is public liability insurance.

instruction.heading: The main types to consider
instruction.body: Public liability insurance covers third-party claims for injury or property damage caused by the work. Workers compensation insurance covers employees for injuries at work. Tools and equipment cover and motor vehicle cover protect the business's assets. Choose the types that match the actual work, the people who will do it and the clients it serves. Then confirm each choice with the insurer or with an adviser who is authorised to give the advice.

instruction.heading: Comparing quotes like for like
instruction.body: Obtain at least two quotes for the same scope of work. Compare the limit of cover, the excess, the exclusions, the work the policy says it covers, any restriction on height, roof or electrical work, the claims process and the renewal terms. A lower premium is not a better policy if it excludes the work you do. Check that the person giving advice is authorised. The ASIC register is the place to check it, and the check should be made on the ASIC site before any advice is accepted.

instruction.heading: Keeping the evidence
instruction.body: Keep a register of each policy with the insurer, the cover type, the limit, the start date, the renewal date and where the document is kept. Send a copy of the current certificate to a client when a job requires it. Renew before the expiry date, because a lapse can end cover for work already in progress. Tell the insurer when an employee, a new service or a new vehicle is added, because undisclosed changes can affect a claim. This lesson does not recommend any insurer or broker.

procedure: List the work you will do, the people who will work with you and the assets you will use.
Match each risk to an insurance type, and leave out any type you are unsure about.
Request at least two quotes for the same scope and record the terms side by side.
Check the exclusions for licensed work, height or roof work, and any service you plan to offer.
Confirm that the adviser is authorised, and read the policy wording before paying.
Record each policy in a register with its renewal date, and file the certificate with the job records when a client needs it.

workedExamples.situation: A handyman plans to clean gutters and carry out minor roof repairs. One quote excludes any work above a stated height.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the handyman accept a roof repair job, given that exclusion?
workedExamples.reasoning: The exclusion means the policy may not cover the roof work, so the handyman must not accept the job on the assumption that cover exists. The options are to ask the insurer in writing whether the work is covered, to change the scope so that it stays within the cover, or to refer the roof work to a trade that holds the right cover and any licence required. The decision turns on the policy wording, which this lesson cannot supply.

equipmentAndPpe: Insurance register with policy numbers, limits, excesses and renewal dates
Scope of work list used for every quote
Certificates of currency filed with the job records

commonErrors.error: Buying the cheapest policy without checking the exclusions for the work offered.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare quotes for the same scope and read the exclusions before paying.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a policy covers licensed work the owner is not licensed to do.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the policy wording and the state licence rules before accepting the work.

commonErrors.error: Letting a policy lapse between jobs.
commonErrors.prevention: Set renewal reminders at least a month before expiry, and log each renewal.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Insurance does not give a licence. This lesson does not grant any licence or permission to perform regulated work.
Ask the client or the authority in writing, and keep the answer on file.

At least two quotes are compared for the same scope, with the exclusions recorded.
The insurance register holds current policy details and a renewal date for every policy.
documentationEvidence: Insurance register with cover type, limit, excess, start date and renewal date
Copy of each current certificate of currency, with the date it was checked
summary: Match insurance types to the risks of the actual work.
Compare quotes for the same scope, and read the exclusions.
Insurance does not give a licence, and certificates and renewal dates must stay current.

knowledgeChecks.question: A policy is cheap, but it excludes the type of work the owner plans to offer. What should the owner do?
options: Buy it, because the price is lower and the cover is probably wide enough for the work
Assume the cover applies in practice and the insurer will pay for any claim
Check the exclusion, then change the scope, obtain written confirmation, or refer the work
Remove the exclusion by telling the client about it and then carry on with the work

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes two insurance quotes comparable?
options: The premium amount alone, and the excess the owner will pay
The same scope of work and the same limits, exclusions and conditions
The brand name of the insurer and the size of the logo on the quote
The date the quote was printed and the name of the agent who sent it

knowledgeChecks.question: What does insurance give a tradesperson?
options: A licence to perform regulated work for any type of trade in the state
A guarantee that clients will pay for every job on the books today
Financial protection for certain claims, under the terms of the policy
Permission to work above a set height and a licence to use power tools
